narrative_purpose: Shows niche partitioning made concrete: three Pandoran herbivores feed at three separated heights in one forest, so coexistence-as-divided-resource is visible at a glance.
subject: A vertical cutaway of a Pandoran forest from ground to high canopy, with three different six-limbed herbivores each feeding in its own clearly separate horizontal band. LOW near the ground: a small slender browser cropping understory shoots. MID-HEIGHT: a taller herd animal feeding on mid-level foliage. HIGH near the canopy: a massive crested grazer reaching up into the high leaves. Each animal sits in its own distinct stratum with clear vertical separation between them.
scene: A glowing bioluminescent forest interior at night, layered foliage at distinct heights, soft haze between layers.
camera: Side-on cutaway view of the forest column, ground at the bottom, canopy at the top.
light: Bioluminescent foliage glowing at each level, rim-lighting each animal; deep indigo shadow between strata.
palette: Void indigo and ocean teal, living-teal foliage glow at each height, a scarce magenta bloom on one high flower, warm kept minimal.
style: Hand-painted naturalist cutaway plate, painterly, reading as a diagram by its layered composition.
detail_level: High on each animal and its feeding level; soft haze separating the bands.
composition: Three stacked horizontal feeding bands with clear vertical gaps, each animal in its own band, dark side margins for callouts.
consistency_notes: Pandoran six-limbed herbivores consistent with the moon's body plan; the teaching point is vertical separation, so keep the bands distinct.
